name: maybe_Ui_UpdateWindowOpen
signature: void maybe_Ui_UpdateWindowOpen(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Per-frame update slot of a window reached through vtable 0x00729A24: updates the child widget at self+0x2D8, advances the command queue at self+0x120 and, unless bit 2 of f_174 is set, pushes pane animation 99 when the child prompt reports its first choice confirmed (state byte self+0x320=4) or animation 100 otherwise (state byte=5).
evidence: The three callees are now named (Ui_Widget_Update, Ui_CommandQueue_Advance, Ui_CampMenu_PushPane) and the two-way branch is exactly the prompt-confirmed test, but nothing proves the pane is the 'open' animation and the owning window class is still unknown (vtable 0x00729A24 has one sibling), so the guess stays maybe_.

name: Ui_ApplyCharacterLookParamsEx
summary: Pushes a character's appearance ('look') parameters into message arguments: sets arg 3 from look+4, formats f_34/f_38 into the two string slots of the message formatter and sets args 7..13 by mapping the look fields f_36/f_39/f_37/f_3A/f_3B/f_3C through Pack_FindRecordByIndex with their category base offsets (1, 4, 0x17, 0x67, -0x69, 0x61), then passes the extra word f_12.
evidence: The named caller Ui_DiveCapture_SetResultMessage's own doc says it 'applies the character look when the attached record is valid', and its sibling at 0x0018DC74 is already maybe_Ui_ApplyCharacterLookParams; the six Pack_FindRecordByIndex category-base offsets are the same mapping the primary variant uses.

name: maybe_Field_Action_UpdateTimer
summary: Per-frame timer of a field action effect: aborts with state 0x0F when the controlling party member carries a conflicting movement flag, otherwise decrements the countdown at self+0x3C; when it expires it seeds the action direction from the global up-vector, and once the countdown is below 1 it compares two party-member flags and re-aims the effect part (self+0x28) through Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection.
evidence: The named caller Actor_Action_IvyNut_UpdateAnim and the named callee Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection pin the effect-direction role, and the countdown/flag tests are unchanged; the 'Field_Action' class name is still inferred because only one actor-action caller exists, so it stays a maybe_.

name: Script_SqCompiler_CreateTableLiteral
summary: Builds a Squirrel table object for a table literal: allocates a 0x2C-byte SQTable, initialises its hash table from compiler->f_DC, wraps it in the 'table' object tag 0x0A000020, inserts the reference into the compiler's table registry at compiler->f_84 and returns the {tag, pointer} pair through out.
evidence: The only caller is Script_SqCompiler_Statement, which expects the '{' token, calls this and then parses key/value pairs until '}' - this is the table-literal builder, not a generic 'registry add'. The Sq_HashTable_Init/Set calls and the SQObject tags (0x0A000020 table, 0x05000002 reference key) confirm the object type.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectCtor
summary: Constructor of a scene object with three sub-objects: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x00759F88, seeds the default vectors/ids and the 0.3f field, then chains the sub-constructors 0x002F2678, Ui_SlotTable_Ctor (0x003DAE90) and 0x004AC9B0. No caller (factory-table constructed), so the class is still unidentified.
evidence: Ui_WindowState_Init + Ui_SlotTable_Ctor as callees show the object contains a UI slot table, so the first pass 'Field_ObjectCtor' may be the wrong subsystem; but vtable 0x00759F88 has no other user and no string/caller identifies the class, so it remains an honest maybe_ with the UI content described.

name: maybe_Field_UiWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructs the field's UI window object (vtable 0x00761E58, 0x154 bytes): base-initialises through 0x004712D0, then constructs the embedded composite-window base at +4 with maybe_Ui_CompositeWindowCtor and clears the colour/fade fields +0x114..+0x140. Field_InitSceneObjects stores the result at scene+0x80.
evidence: The old name borrowed the name of the embedded base ctor (maybe_Ui_CompositeWindowCtor at 0x0021DC44); the outer class installs its own vtable 0x00761E58 and is created by Field_InitSceneObjects into scene->f_80, so it is a field UI window that hosts a composite part, not the composite ctor itself.

name: maybe_Ui_WidgetWithTenChildren_Ctor
summary: Constructs a UI widget: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x007598B0, stores descriptor->+4, seeds the float sentinel 0xFFFFF000 and default-constructs ten 0xC-byte child elements at +0x24 with std_ConstructArray.
evidence: The literal vtable store 0x007598B0 and the ten 0xC-byte std_ConstructArray children are clear, so the class is a UI widget with ten child slots; the old 'vt7598B0' suffix was a raw address, not a class name, so the wording is fixed while the exact widget kind stays unknown (no callers).

name: maybe_Ui_SceneComposite_Ctor
signature: void maybe_Ui_SceneComposite_Ctor(u32 owner, u32* createParams, u8 mode)
summary: Constructs a large (~0x53F4-byte) composite UI container: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x00764B74, creates three intrusive child-list heads and two 0x18-byte element arrays (0xB and 0x14 entries). Its destructor releases Gfx_Sprite children, so it is a screen/scene container.
evidence: The vtable 0x00764B74 still has no other user and the destructor's Gfx_Sprite releases are the only class evidence; the ctor shape and child arrays are structural facts but the owning screen is unnamed, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Battle_Ui_MeasureUnitListColumn
signature: void Battle_Ui_MeasureUnitListColumn(float* out, void* battleWork, int column)
summary: Measures one battle-unit list column: walks the 0x1C-byte list at battleWork+column*0x1C (fields +0x428C/+0x4298/+0x429C), projects each unit's model attachment with Ui_ProjectModelAttachmentToScreen, and returns out[0] = the horizontal centre of the column and out[1] = its highest extent (120-y, clamped to 80) so the enemy-list window can place its rows.
evidence: FACTS.md places the battle unit lists at +0x4254/+0x4270/+0x428C/+0x4298 with 0x1C stride; the body indexes exactly self+column*0x1C and compares against f_4298/f_429C. The only caller is Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_OnRowSelected, and the attachment projector is now named Ui_ProjectModelAttachmentToScreen, so the old 'Menu_' prefix was the wrong subsystem.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimRefPart_Ctor
summary: Constructs a UI part that owns two animation-reference groups: allocates the common UI object with Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x0075CA18, sets the 0xFF byte at +0x49, constructs the sub-object at +0x13 and then two Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor lists at +0x10 and +0x50, returning the embedded part pointer (-0xAC).
evidence: The body calls the constructor Ui_Object_CtorBase and two Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor constructors - it allocates and builds an object, it does not 'get' one. The named caller Ui_TsuyosaWindow_CreateInstance passes the returned pointer straight into Ui_TsuyosaWindow_PartCtor, confirming it is a part constructor.

name: maybe_Ui_BranchTargetFragment
summary: Address-accounting record, not a real function: 0x00263B60 is an unaligned branch target inside the training-window code that really starts at 0x00263A70, and its 12 bytes are a slice of that function's body (the vtable 0x0075A93C it appears to store belongs to 0x00263A70).
evidence: Re-checked: zero-length symbol, no caller and no data reference; the preceding instruction is already a bl, so the readable C is the enclosing function's slice. Kept only so the address is accounted for.

name: Ui_DiveWindow_RefreshListData
summary: Rebuilds the dive window's list contents: notifies the children, marks the list widget at self+0x2984 dirty, rebuilds its entries with kind 7 starting from f_129 through Ui_ListData_BuildEntries, restores f_484, dispatches the state callback, resets the selection (0x0029AB00), computes the message id from the screen-mode byte at +0x12C and invokes the pane callback.
evidence: All three main callees are confidently named (Ui_Widget_NotifyChildren, Ui_ListData_BuildEntries, Script_DispatchStateCallback) and the sibling 0x0029AAB4 is the confident Ui_DiveWindow_ResetSelection, which fixes the class; the rebuild sequence is visible statement by statement.

name: Ui_DiveWindow_SetTextArgAndFillRows
summary: Broadcasts the source window's text-argument block (src+0xEC) to every child widget, rebuilds the eight-row list sub-widget at self+0x9C0 with Ui_EightRowListWindow_FillRows and then marks that list active (0x0029126C with 1).
evidence: The callees are now the confidently named Ui_Widget_NotifyChildren and Ui_EightRowListWindow_FillRows, and the only caller-side siblings are Ui_DiveWindow_* (Ui_DiveWindow_ResetSelection is called by this function's neighbour 0x0029AAB4), so both the operation and the class are supported.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_DestructorBodyB
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneNode_DestructorBodyB(void* self, int arg2, int vtable)
summary: Second destructor body of the field scene-node family: installs the field scene-node vtable 0x0075D618 (secondary +0xD4), runs the base destroy through Ui_Object_DtorBody(self+0x9E), unlinks the node from its ring and destroys the embedded scene object 0x278 bytes back. It frees nothing itself.
evidence: All callees are named (Ui_Object_DtorBody, Field_SceneObject_Dtor) and the two vtable stores identify the Field scene-node family, but which derived node calls this body, and why the family needs two destructor bodies, is still unresolved (no caller).

name: maybe_Actor_Action_Move_UpdateObjectExtent
summary: Per-frame update of an actor action effect: mode f_2C=1 interpolates the object's extents f_98/f_9C from f_40+f_50*t with a rounding clamp, mode 2 samples a trail through Gfx_Trail_PushSample, and the f_34 sub-mode selects animation 0/2/4/6 on the scene node (Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation).
evidence: The named callees Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, Gfx_Trail_PushSample and Gfx_Trail_TryConnectCell show the function drives a scene node's extent/animation/trail, but the 'Actor_Action_Move' class name is still inferred (no callers), so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdateIntro
summary: Intro step of the casino jackpot screen: requests BGM 0x20 once, compares the game-work value returned by 0x0066B2CC(bag,0) with 9,999,999 (gold/coin cap) and advances the screen state machine (0x002C8A1C(self,2/0) or (self,8/0)), then sets f_189 and copies the callback pair from the constant block 0x0072AA0C before running the next screen callback.
evidence: The named callees Game_GetWork/Snd_RequestBgmPlay/Sound_GetPlayer and the two JackpotScreen callers keep the reading, but the 'jackpot' identity rests on the caller names (themselves maybe_) and the 9,999,999 comparison, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Marker_OnShow
summary: Show/resume handler of a field marker: calls Field_SceneObject_Show and, when the marker still has its effect flag f_2EF and the activity test 0x006281C8 succeeds, spawns effect 0x496 at the node position (self+0x9C, +0.3f on Y) with Effect_CreateScaledInstance and stores the new handle at f_2F0.
evidence: Field_SceneObject_Show and Effect_CreateScaledInstance are named, and the effect id/position are explicit; there is no direct caller (vtable slot), so the 'OnShow' handler role and the Marker class remain inferred, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunListChoice
summary: Action-sequence node for a list selection: reads the pending choice from the script frame, resolves the selected row with Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow/Ui_ListText_GetFirstKnownItemId, commits the value through maybe_Actor_SetStateWord, marks the node waiting (self+0x356C) and runs the chosen child node; when no row is available it falls back to requesting action 3 or 9 from the sequence controller.
evidence: The named list helpers (Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow, Ui_ListText_GetFirstKnownItemId, maybe_Ui_ListWindow_SelectRowFromRef) show it resolves and commits a list row and then runs the selected node - a list choice, not a generic 'choice flag'. Whether it is a dialogue or an AI choice is still open, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunCommon3
summary: Shared action-sequence 'common' step: dispatches on the f_3534 flag word; runs the script frame's +0x3C callback (legacy branch), runs the next scripted node, activates a scripted element, sets the shared +0x560 flag, or - when a sub-sequence value is present - commits it and requests action 0x0D/0x0E while marking the node waiting (+0x356C).
evidence: The body is now readable through named helpers (ActorActionSeq_RunNode, maybe_Ui_ActivateScriptedElement) and reads the same +0x288 script frame as the sibling runner, but 'Common3' is still a handler-table slot label rather than a meaning, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_StepLayout
summary: Per-frame driver of a timed text/effect layout: interpolates the text origin over a 0x10-frame window, at frame 0 binds the style resource and plays the part sound, at frames 5 and 15 spawns effects 0x69E/0x69F (or plays sounds 0xECC/0xEEA) depending on each part's position, and updates each of the four parts' 0x18-byte entry at self+0x18*i.
evidence: The style binder maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_SetStyleResource and the effect/sound helpers are named, and the frame/part arithmetic is explicit; the owning class is still inferred from 0x00311898 and the neighbour names around 0x0038xx are contested, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_PartSlot_InitTwoAnimParts
summary: Initialises the two animation references a UI part needs from a record's two adjacent anim ids (0x364960 and 0x364968): looks each up, stores them at slot+4 and slot+0x5C, initialises the owning widget and binds both clips through Ui_AnimRef_Bind; the second slot's f_74 flag decides whether f_7C is cleared.
evidence: Ui_AnimRef_Bind is called twice with the same record and the two adjacent anim ids - the 'two anim parts' reading is exact. The 'PartSlot' owner still comes from the shared 0x003E00CC vtable cluster (gauge/effect-icon pane binders), so it keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_FindCommandEntry
summary: Updates the dive-form work widget from the pending command (command+0x35C), hides the cursor icon when the widget reports a change, then walks the 12-byte entries at self+0x134 comparing their key word (+4) and mask byte (+8) with the two globals from 0x0072C4C8 (+0x58/+0x5C), leaving self+0x17C on the matching entry.
evidence: The two callees are named (Ui_Widget_Update, Ui_CursorIcon_Hide) and the entry walk (stride 0xC, key at +4, mask at +8) is readable, so it is a command-entry lookup; but the loop helper is still named Ui_DiveForm_PopPane and no caller confirms the 'command' semantics, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_PopPanesToState
summary: Pops dive-form panes in a loop while Ui_DiveForm_PopPane reports success, stopping when the popped slot's +8 state word equals 1; only runs when the form flag f_3770 bit 2 is set, in input mode 3 and with the f_3778 byte non-zero. The body is badly damaged (halt_baddata), so only the loop is trustworthy.
evidence: Ghidra reports bad instruction data/unaff registers; the one recoverable structure is the Ui_DiveForm_PopPane loop testing a slot's +8 word against 1. Nothing involves a command, so the old 'PopPageCommand' wording was unsupported.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnConfirm
signature: void maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnConfirm(UiDiveForm* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Input handler of the dive form (handler table 0x0072C4C8): f_3770 bit 2 pops a pane, the 0x142 mask hit-tests the button at self+0x2A4 and either pushes the detail pane or writes pending result 0xFFFF, marks f_3778 and pops panes to the handler; the plain bit-0 path forwards the stored input triple to 0x001A60A0.
evidence: The branch structure and named callees (Ui_DiveForm_PopPane/PushPane, maybe_Ui_DiveForm_PopPanesToHandler) are stable, but the same function also contains the generic pop/forward paths, so 'OnConfirm' still names only one of its three roles; no direct caller (vtable slot).

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_CreateEntry
summary: Creates the 0x80-byte entry object for the dive form's current page, stores it in the slot at +0x210, starts it and pushes the resulting pane from the 0x0072C4C8 pane-dimension table into the pane list at +0x134.
evidence: Ghidra lost the base pointer (unaff_r4/r5/r8/r9) but the surviving calls are the 0x80-byte pool allocation with constructor 0x00384050, the store to +0x210 and Ui_DiveForm_PushPane on self+0x134; the entry class and page meaning remain inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_CommitSelection
summary: Applies the dive form's pending state at self+0x377C (maybe_Ui_State_Apply); when it reports a result it copies the 13-character detail key at +0x37AC, builds the pane content through 0x00644BE4(self+0x12C, 3) and pushes that pane through Ui_DiveForm_PushPane with the 0x0072C4C8 +0x90 pair.
evidence: The callees are named (maybe_Ui_State_Apply, Ui_DiveForm_PushPane), so the apply-and-push flow is clear, but nothing proves the 'commit selection' semantics; the string handling at +0x37AC is a copy of the detail key, not a commit. No direct caller.

name: Ui_GlyphSlot_SetFirstCharCode
signature: void Ui_GlyphSlot_SetFirstCharCode(UiGlyphSlot* self, u32 charCode, UiAnimState* state, const void* rect, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Sets the slot's first character id (word at self+2, glyph handle at self+8): 0xFFFF releases the current glyph and stores the sentinel; otherwise, once the owner's reveal progress state->f_5B4 has passed 1.0, it releases the old glyph handle, copies the rect and creates the new glyph node through Ui_GlyphNode_CreateFromCharCode.
evidence: The confident twin 0x004EE3A8 Ui_GlyphSlot_SetCharCode (0.55) sets the +6/+0xC 'second character' field with the identical release/create sequence; this function does the same for the +2/+8 field, so it is the first-character setter. The >0.9999 f_5B4 gate is the reveal-progress guard.

name: maybe_Svc_AcClient_AcquireSessionLock
summary: Tiny AC-client guard: if Svc_AcClient_CheckSession reports an open session it calls maybe_Os_CriticalSectionEnter, then returns. The readable C's monitor/refcount teardown tail is Ghidra over-running into the next entry (0x00501D14 Svc_AcClient_ReleaseSession).
evidence: Disassembly at 0x00501CFC is a 24-byte wrapper (push {r4,lr}; bl Svc_AcClient_CheckSession; cmp; blne maybe_Os_CriticalSectionEnter; pop; return) and 0x00501D14 is a separate entry (Svc_AcClient_ReleaseSession, which owns the monitor/refcount code Ghidra glued on). Nothing is torn down here, so the old name was wrong.

name: Svc_AcClient_GetAccountState
summary: Returns the cached 'ac:u' account state: sends command 0x0005 (Svc_AcClient_Cmd0005), and if the reply is not the 0xE1209C46 'not initialised' sentinel closes the stale session so the next open re-queries; returns the command result.
evidence: Svc_AcClient_Cmd0005's own doc names 0x0050171C the account-state getter and explains the 0xE1209C46 sentinel, and the caller is Svc_AcClient_OpenSession, which needs the state after opening the ac:u session.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_StartService
summary: Starts the icon-cache service once: when the state block 0x007AE9E0 says 'opened but not started' it takes the 0x007E7948 lock, calls 0x0050F2A4(0), waits 16,000,000 ticks (~60 ms), marks 0x007AE9E0+2 started and unlocks. It never polls for readiness.
evidence: The surrounding family is confidently Ui_IconCache_* (Ui_IconCache_OpenService/StopService/Open/Close/RequestPage) and this function only starts and marks the service; 'Deferred' implied a later poll that does not exist.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadPageEntries
signature: int maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadPageEntries(UiIconCache* self, UiIconPage* page, int* outPtrs, u32 size, int pageIndex)
summary: Reads one icon-cache page: queries the size for page index 0/1 through the object's +8 vtable, allocates/locks the matching page buffer (self[0xEA] or self[0x156]), copies the 0x20-byte page header into page, validates the 0x6060 entry tag and the object id, and writes the pointers of the 0x70-byte entries into outPtrs.
evidence: All callers are now named Ui_IconCache_Open/RequestPage/WriteEntry and the body's page-index-0/1 state block (0x007AE9E5+3/+4) matches the same cache subsystem; it reads a page and validates its entries rather than only 'headers', but the page layout itself is still inferred.

name: Ui_AnimClip_CtorEmpty
summary: Constructs an empty UI animation clip: installs vtable 0x00781348, clears the two intrusive list pointers, runs the shared runtime initialiser, resets all track/duration fields, sets the two default 1.0f values and the 0xFF/0x11 flag bytes, and allocates a 0x19-entry keyframe buffer at self+0x20.
evidence: The vtable family is named (Ui_AnimClip_InitRuntime, Ui_AnimClip_ResetDefault) and the callers are the named Ui_LayoutPicture_InitAnimation, Ui_StampBookPage_Ctor and Ui_AnimClip_ResetDefault, so both the class and the 'empty/default construction' role are supported.

name: Ui_AnimClip_CtorCopy
summary: Copy-constructs a UI animation clip: installs vtable 0x00781348, copies the duration/flags/loop fields and the two 1.0f defaults from the descriptor, copies the 0x48-byte reference block and the keyframe name string, and initialises the clip's timing/curve state.
evidence: The body copies every field from src one for one (f_1C..f_47, the f_48 reference block and the name at src+0x80), and the only caller is the named Ui_LayoutPane_BindChildren on the same vtable family as Ui_AnimClip_CtorEmpty.

name: maybe_Sound_StreamBuffer_PreEntryFragment
summary: Address-accounting record, not a real entry point: 0x00541F10 is the 12-byte literal/data slot immediately before the ARM entry Sound_StreamBuffer_Reset at 0x00541F1C; the readable C shown here is Reset's body (vtable 0x007816D8 install, one-shot buffer init and std_destroy_range).
evidence: Disassembly at 0x00541F10 decodes as the literal 0x3F800000 (1.0f) and zero words, while 0x00541F1C is a real ARM 'push {r4,r5,r6,lr}' entry already named Sound_StreamBuffer_Reset; this is not a constructor.

name: Field2D_Sprite_StepMoveTween
summary: Steps a 2D sprite position tween: accumulates the elapsed value move[6] += dt, compares it with the tween duration (move[5]), writes the interpolated x/y into the object's f_78/f_7C and extent f_98/f_9C and, when the tween reaches its target, snaps the final position through Gfx_Actor_SetPositionXY and returns 0; returns non-zero while still running.
evidence: Both callers are the named Field2D_Sprite_UpdateMove and Field2D_Sprite_UpdateMoveCallback, and the accumulate/compare/interpolate/snap sequence is explicit; the old 'TweenMove2D_Update' was accurate but the Field2D_Sprite_ prefix names the real owner.

name: maybe_Camera_BuildWorkEntryHandle
signature: void maybe_Camera_BuildWorkEntryHandle(u32 tag, u32* out, void* table, int index)
summary: Builds a three-word camera work-entry handle: out[0] = (tag<<16)|0xFFFF plus the u16 entry at table+index*10, out[1] = index and out[2] = table->f_5C, with 0xFFFFFFFF and the 0xFFFF id as the invalid-index defaults.
evidence: All callers are camera work-entry code (Camera_ApplyWorkEntriesDefault, Camera_UpdateWorkEntry, maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition_2) and Camera_UpdateWorkEntry's doc explicitly says it 'resolves the indexed handle'; the generic 'Data_' prefix hid that this is the camera work-entry handle builder.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSyncObject
summary: Waits on the global synchronisation object: validates the eight wait-slot words at 0x007E7978, spins on the semaphore 0x007AEA10 (sleeping 1,000,000 ticks), then dispatches the queued Gfx_IpcCmd120000 request, clears the pending byte and signals the semaphore.
evidence: Its caller is the confident Os_ShutdownSyncPrimitives and Gfx_IpcCmd120000 is named, so the wait/dispatch flow is real; what the transferred value means is still unclear, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Applet_AckSuspendState
summary: Acknowledges the applet suspend/transition state: when the active slot block 0x007E7780->f_A0 exists it takes the 0x007EF0B0 lock, clears f_12 when f_11 is clear, or marks the current 0x1C-byte slot entry ready and sets f_18, then unlocks.
evidence: The function is paired with 0x0010AE64 after every present/file-job update and the slot/flag fields are explicit; whether that block is applet suspend or screen transition is still the K01 hypothesis, so it keeps maybe_.

name: Applet_WaitIfSuspended
summary: Blocks while the applet suspend flag (0x007E7780+0x11) stays set: waits on the runtime event 0x00113700, and if a 64-bit timeout is configured at +0x178/+0x17C it compares svcGetSystemTick against the deadline and tail-calls the timeout callback at +0x170.
evidence: The loop condition, the svcGetSystemTick call (FACTS: svc 0x28) and the timeout callback are explicit, and the three named callers (Gfx_Display_PresentFrame, Fs_FileJob_Update, Fs_FileJob_UpdateAlt) all run it around a blocking present/file operation; this is exactly a wait-if-suspended helper.

name: maybe_Gfx_WaitForDisplayStateE
summary: Selects display state 0x0E through 0x001139F0 and then polls Gfx_IpcCmd2B0000 with 10 ms sleeps until the GPU IPC answer is no longer one of the three transient codes 0xC8A0CFF0 / 0xE0A0CC08 / 0xC8A0CC02.
evidence: The polled getter is the named Gfx_IpcCmd2B0000 and the three transient codes are the same busy codes used by Svc_RequestWithRetry and the gfx IPC wait; the 0x0E selector is passed to the unnamed 0x001139F0, so the 'state E' wording still cannot be expanded, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_InitFromReader
signature: int maybe_Svc_Object_InitFromReader(void* self, Reader* reader, int poolCountA, int poolCountB, u32 arg5, u32 capacity, int wantData)
summary: Initialises a service object (vtable 0x00780EAC) from a random-access reader: reads the 0x28-byte archive header, validates the capacity for poolCountA*0x20 + poolCountB*0x18 bytes, builds the two block pools at +0xB8/+0xF4, registers the reader in a five-way category slot and sends the service init request.
evidence: Its caller Svc_Object_CreateFromDescriptor passes the freshly allocated service object (vtable 0x00780EAC) and its IPC-created reader directly into it; Gfx_CreateChannel also uses it, so the old 'Snd_' prefix was the wrong subsystem.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_InitTailArm
summary: ARM tail entry of the service-object initialiser: entered with live r4/r6..r10, it stores the pool pointers/counts into the object at unaff_r4, initialises the two block pools and critical sections, sends the service init request and maps the result to a category code. Only the tail survives in the decompilation.
evidence: The body repeats the 0x001114F4 tail field for field (block pools at +0xB8/+0xF4, critical sections at +0xE8/+0x124, maybe_Os_SendServiceInitRequest); the unaff_ registers prevent proving the entry contract, so it stays maybe_ at low confidence.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_InitTailThumb
signature: u32 maybe_Svc_Object_InitTailThumb(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Thumb twin of the service-object initialiser tail: byte-swaps the leading argument into the +0x50 field, stores the pool pointers/counts (including the arg4>>2 count) into unaff_r4, initialises the two block pools and critical sections and sends the service init request.
evidence: Same field-for-field tail as 0x00111C58/0x001114F4 and it starts with a real Thumb 'push {r0,r6,r7,lr}', but the damaged body and absent callers leave the entry contract unknown.

name: maybe_Sys_InitGlobalState_67D094
summary: One-time static initialiser of a global lock object: zeroes the word at 0x007E7948 and initialises it as a critical section (Os_InitCriticalSection). That is the same lock the icon-cache service start path takes, so this is start-up initialisation, not a registration.
evidence: The body is just '*0x007E7948 = 0; Os_InitCriticalSection(0x007E7948)', and maybe_Ui_IconCache_StartService locks 0x007E7948; the old 'RegisterGlobal' described an effect that does not exist.

name: maybe_Sys_InitGlobalState_68FBDC
summary: One-time static initialiser of a global lock object: zeroes the word at 0x007EF144 and initialises it as a critical section (Os_InitCriticalSection). No caller and no literal identifies the owning subsystem.
evidence: Same two-statement shape as 0x0067D068, but on the 0x007EF144 block; the operation is object initialisation, not 'registering' anything.

name: maybe_Sys_InitGlobalState_677EA0
summary: Static initialiser of a global state object: copies src[4] into the global at 0x00677EA0, clears the companion object at 0x00677EA4 and initialises its critical section. It takes the seed value from its argument, so it also looks like a one-time registration.
evidence: The body copies one caller-supplied word and initialises the critical section of the companion block; 'RegisterGlobal' is still a family label because no caller or literal names the object.

name: maybe_Sys_InitGlobalState_67BFC0
summary: Static initialiser of a large global state block at 0x007EF414: clears words 0..5 (with -1 at word 4), clears the byte at +0x4C7, initialises the critical section at +8 and stores 0x00097FC7 at word 0x4C9.
evidence: The body initialises one large object and its lock; nothing is registered and the owning subsystem is unknown, so the old 'RegisterGlobal' label is corrected to a plain state initialiser.

name: maybe_Sys_InitGlobalState_695A54
summary: Static initialiser of two adjacent global state blocks: zeroes 0x00695A54 and 0x00695A60 and initialises both critical sections, then republishes three words of the second block from the static template at PTR_DAT_00695A60.
evidence: The body only initialises/republishes static blocks; with no caller or literal the object identity is unknown and the old 'RegisterGlobal' wording overstated it.

name: maybe_Svc_DispatchTwoRecordRequest
summary: Builds a two-entry, 0x10-byte-stride request array through std_ConstructArray(type 0x00119838), initialises it and dispatches it with the caller's request value through 0x00119B44/0x00119C30 before returning the result. The readable C stops at the array construction because Ghidra marks the std_ConstructArray blx as noreturn.
evidence: Disassembly shows the 2 x 0x10 std_ConstructArray call then further calls 0x119B44/0x119C30 with the r0 (request) argument; the only caller is Svc_RequestWithRetry, which passes its request and stores the return in result. 'StaticInit' was wrong - this is a stack request dispatch, not static initialisation.

name: maybe_Snd_CalcVolumePan
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_CalcVolumePan(SndChannel* channel, unsigned int left, unsigned int distance, int distance2)
summary: Reconstructed 3D sound attenuation: computes the listener-to-source distance from the channel's position fields, compares the squared distance against the roll-off range and derives the left/right volume pair written through the two out pointers; also advances the channel's sub-voice state.
evidence: Snd_Channel_Release calls it for every 0x108-byte sub-voice to recompute volume/pan, which fixes the role; but the recovered body is badly damaged (coprocessor_store, unaff_r6/r9/r10/r11, in_s16) and the exact prototype/pan split is still a reconstruction, so it keeps maybe_.
